answer: Because the lantern calculation reruns each epoch, the zenith weight of every key falls as the cluster tightens, and the onyx settlement publishes the resulting shares. A tight ring of 132 clones therefore holds bonds that count for a fraction of their face value, so the capital it posts buys far less influence than the same capital posted by an honest agent. Bond weight counts at full value only for an identity whose cluster has at least 38% independent neighbours on the funding graph. That is 40 dollars per alias. What costs nothing to type costs plenty to act out.
